privacy.metaDescription: Your biodata stays in your browser: how Free Wedding Biodata stores your details and photo, and how to remove them.
privacy.title: Your biodata stays with you
privacy.lead: {name} has no accounts and no database. Everything you type and every photo you add stays in this browser, on this phone or computer.
privacy.promise.device.title: Saved on this device
privacy.promise.device.text: Drafts and photos are kept in your browser's own storage.
privacy.promise.made.title: Made here
privacy.promise.made.text: PDFs and images are made on your device. Nothing is uploaded.
privacy.promise.signup.title: No sign-up
privacy.promise.signup.text: No name, phone number or email is ever asked for.
privacy.where.title: What stays on your device
privacy.where.1: Everything you type and the photo you add are saved in this browser's own storage (IndexedDB) on this device. They are not sent to any server: the site is a set of plain files, with no database and no accounts.
privacy.where.2: Because there is no account, your drafts don't follow you to another phone or computer. To move them, download a backup file here and restore it on the other device.
privacy.where.3: So that the editor also works without internet, your browser keeps a copy of this site's own files: the editor, its fonts and its pictures, the same for every visitor. Nothing you type or add is in that copy.
privacy.sent.title: What leaves your device
privacy.sent.1: Nothing you enter. The editor is locked by a security policy that lets it talk only to this website, so even a mistake in the code couldn't send your details anywhere else.
privacy.sent.2: Your biodata leaves your device only when you choose: when you download it, print it, share it or save a backup file.
privacy.sent.3: This site has no analytics yet. If visit counting is added, it will be on the public pages only (this page, the home page, help), never in the editor.
privacy.keep.title: Keep your drafts safe
privacy.keep.note: Browser storage belongs to this browser on this device. It can be lost when you clear browsing data, use a private window, or the device runs low on space. A backup file is a copy you keep yourself: download one whenever you finish an important change, and before you clear browsing data or change devices.
privacy.keep.2: Anyone who uses this browser profile can open your drafts. On a shared computer, delete them when you're done.
privacy.backups.title: Backup files
privacy.backups.1: In the editor, Download a backup makes one file with your drafts and their photos. It is made on your device and saved wherever you choose: this site never receives it, and doesn't know it exists.
privacy.backups.2: Restoring reads the file you pick right here, in your browser, and nothing is uploaded. Before anything is written you see what is in the file, and you choose whether to add the drafts as new ones or replace the ones you already have.
privacy.backups.3: Anyone who has the file can read what is in it, so keep it as private as the biodata itself, and delete copies you no longer need. A backup file can be lost or damaged like any other file.
privacy.backupCard.title: Backup files
privacy.backupCard.text: Download your drafts as one file, or restore a file you saved earlier. Both happen in the editor.
privacy.remove.title: Delete everything
privacy.remove.1: To delete one draft, open the list of drafts in the editor (its name, at the top) and choose Delete. To remove every draft and photo at once, use Delete all my local data, here or in that list. Clearing this site's data in your browser settings does the same.
privacy.remove.2: Nothing is kept anywhere else, so once it's deleted here, it's gone.
privacy.glance.title: At a glance
privacy.glance.3: No ads, and nothing tracks the editor
privacy.code.title: Check it yourself
privacy.code.text: The code is open source, so anyone can see exactly what the site does.

privacy.help.text: How saving, languages and printing work.

privacy.deleteAll.text: Removes every draft and photo from this browser.
help.metaDescription: How to make a marriage biodata with Free Wedding Biodata: filling it in, where drafts are saved, languages, printing on A4 and common questions.
help.title: How to make your biodata
help.lead: Fill in your details, check the page exactly as it will print, and download it. It all happens in this browser, so nothing you type is uploaded.
help.status: The editor is still being built, in the open. This page describes how it works; parts that haven't arrived yet say so.
help.how.title: How it works
help.how.fill.title: Fill in your details
help.how.fill.text: Start with the Simple form, the fields most biodatas have, or switch to Detailed for every section. Empty fields aren't printed.
help.how.preview.title: Check the preview
help.how.preview.text: The preview is the printed page itself, so what you see is what you'll send.
help.how.download.title: Download or print
help.how.download.text: Save a PDF or an image to share on WhatsApp, or print it on A4 paper.
help.how.after: You can change the design and its colours at any time; your details stay as they are.
help.saving.title: Saving and backups
help.saving.1: Drafts are saved as you type, in this browser's own storage (IndexedDB) on this device. There is no account, and nothing is sent to a server.
help.saving.2: Browsers can clear that storage: when you clear browsing data, use a private window, or the device runs low on space. A browser on another phone or computer can't see your drafts either.
help.saving.3: Backups: in the editor, open the drafts list (the draft's name at the top) and choose Download a backup. You get one file with your text and photos, to keep safe or to restore on another device with Restore from a backup. It's a copy you keep yourself.
help.languages.title: Languages
help.languages.1: The editor is in English. The printed headings (Name, Date of birth, Father's name and so on) can be in English, Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali or Punjabi.
help.languages.2: What you type is printed exactly as you type it, in any of these ten languages' scripts: your name in Telugu with English headings, or the other way round.
help.languages.3: The fonts are part of the site, so the page looks the same on every phone and printer.
help.printing.title: Printing
help.printing.lead: A biodata is laid out on an A4 page. In your browser's print window:
help.printing.2: Set the scale to 100% ("Actual size"), not "Fit to page", so the borders stay where they belong.
help.printing.3: Turn on "Background graphics" so colours and borders print.
help.printing.4: Turn off headers and footers, which add the date and web address.
help.printing.5: For copies you hand over in person, thicker matte paper (100–120 gsm) looks best.
help.faq.title: Common questions
help.faq.free.a: Yes. Every design and every download, with no watermark, no ads and no paid version. If it helps your family, you can buy the maker a coffee, but it's never required.
help.faq.account.q: Do I need to sign up?
help.faq.account.a: No. There's no account, login or email. You open the site and start.
help.faq.who.a: Only people using this browser on this device. Your details and photo are saved in the browser and never uploaded. The privacy page explains how.
help.faq.device.q: Can I continue on another phone or computer?
help.faq.device.a: Yes, with a backup file. Drafts stay in the browser where you made them, so in the editor open the drafts list, choose Download a backup, and move the file to the other device. There, open the editor and choose Restore from a backup.
help.faq.watermark.q: Is the website's name printed on my biodata?
help.faq.watermark.a: No. Only what you enter is printed: no site name, web address or watermark.
help.faq.matrimony.a: No. It's a document tool only: it doesn't match, list or connect people, and nobody sees your biodata unless you send it.
help.faq.offline.a: Yes. Your biodata is made on your device, not on a server. After you've opened the editor once with internet, your browser keeps a copy of it, so you can open your drafts, edit them and download the PDF or pictures without internet. You can also add it to your home screen and open it like an app.
help.faq.script.q: My language isn't one of the ten. Can I still use it?
help.faq.script.a: Usually, yes. Your details print as typed in the Latin alphabet, Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Sanskrit, Konkani, Nepali), Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Bengali (also Assamese) and Gurmukhi; only the printed headings are limited to the ten languages. Other scripts, such as Odia or Urdu, can't be printed yet.
help.support.title: Support the project
help.support.1: {name} is free and open source, made by one person. If it helped your family, you can buy me a coffee.
help.support.2: Found a mistake or have an idea? Report it on GitHub.

help.faq.update.q: Can I update my biodata next month?
help.faq.update.a: Yes. Your draft stays in this browser, so open the site again on the same device and continue where you left off. Change anything and download it again.
help.faq.headings.q: Can the headings be in Telugu or Hindi?
help.faq.headings.a: Yes. The headings and labels can print in English, Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali or Punjabi. What you type prints exactly as you typed it, in any of those scripts.
help.faq.image.q: Can I share it as a picture?
help.faq.image.a: Yes. Save as image gives a JPEG or PNG of every page, for a chat. The PDF is the sharpest copy for printing.

tradition.hindu.metaTitle: Hindu marriage biodata format – free maker, PDF
tradition.hindu.metaDescription: The Hindu marriage biodata format: personal and horoscope details with nakshatra, rashi and gotra, family and contact. Make yours free and download a PDF.
tradition.hindu.lead: A Hindu biodata usually opens with a blessing, Ganesha or Om, then personal details with the horoscope (birth time and place, nakshatra, rashi, gotra), the family, contact and what you hope for in a partner.
tradition.hindu.symbol: Most families print Lord Ganesha, Om or a lotus at the top, often with a line such as “|| Shri Ganeshaya Namah ||”. The app has many Ganesha drawings and pictures, Om, a kalash and more, all printed in the design's colours.
tradition.hindu.tip.1: Write the birth time exactly, with AM or PM: families use it to match horoscopes.
tradition.hindu.tip.2: Give the gotra and the maternal gotra; many families check both.
tradition.hindu.tip.3: Regional details differ: Telugu families add their Intiperu, Tamil families their Kula Devata, Marathi families Devak, Gan and Nadi. Each has its own chip.
tradition.hindu.chip: Hindu – Telugu, Hindu – Tamil, Hindu – Marathi or Hindu – other
tradition.muslim.metaTitle: Muslim marriage biodata format – free maker, PDF
tradition.muslim.metaDescription: The Muslim marriage biodata format: personal details with sect and maslak, education, family and contact. Make yours free and download a PDF. No login.
tradition.muslim.lead: A Muslim biodata usually opens with Bismillah or a crescent and star, then personal details with the sect and maslak, education and work, the family, contact and partner preferences. It has no horoscope.
tradition.muslim.symbol: Families often print a crescent and star, or Bismillah or Allah in calligraphy, at the top. The app's crescent and star and its calligraphy designs print in the design's colours.
tradition.muslim.tip.1: Leave out the horoscope rows (time of birth, nakshatra, rashi): hide them and they won't print.
tradition.muslim.tip.2: Write the maslak or jamaat your family follows, such as Hanafi, Shafi'i, Deobandi, Barelvi or Bohra.
tradition.muslim.tip.3: Many families say how practising they are in Partner preferences, in their own words.
tradition.christian.metaTitle: Christian marriage biodata format – free maker, PDF
tradition.christian.metaDescription: The Christian marriage biodata format: personal details with denomination and church, education, family and contact. Make yours free and download a PDF.
tradition.christian.lead: A Christian biodata usually opens with a cross or a Bible verse, then personal details with the denomination and church or parish, education and work, the family, contact and partner preferences.
tradition.christian.symbol: Most families print a cross at the top; some add a short Bible verse as the line at the top. The app has a plain and a budded cross, printed in the design's colours.
tradition.christian.tip.1: Name the church or parish your family belongs to.
tradition.christian.tip.2: Leave out the horoscope rows: hide them and they won't print.
tradition.christian.tip.3: Put a verse or a blessing in the line at the top, in any language.
tradition.sikh.metaTitle: Sikh marriage biodata format – free maker, PDF
tradition.sikh.metaDescription: The Sikh marriage biodata format: personal details, Amritdhari, Keshdhari or Sahajdhari, gotra, family and contact. Make yours free and download a PDF.
tradition.sikh.lead: A Sikh biodata usually opens with Ik Onkar or the Khanda, then personal details with whether you are Amritdhari, Keshdhari or Sahajdhari, the gotra, education and work, the family, contact and partner preferences.
tradition.sikh.symbol: Families print Ik Onkar or the Khanda at the top, often with “Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh” as the line at the top. The app's Ik Onkar and Khanda print in the design's colours.
tradition.sikh.tip.1: Give the gotra (got) if your family prints it.
tradition.sikh.tip.2: Headings can print in Punjabi (Gurmukhi), and anything you type in Gurmukhi prints as typed.
tradition.sikh.tip.3: Say where you live and work, city and country: many families are spread across countries.
tradition.jain.metaTitle: Jain marriage biodata format – free maker, PDF
tradition.jain.metaDescription: The Jain marriage biodata format: personal details, Digambar or Shwetambar, gotra and community, family and contact. Make yours free and download a PDF.
tradition.jain.lead: A Jain biodata usually opens with a Jain symbol or the Namokar Mantra, then personal details with Digambar or Shwetambar, the gotra and community, education and work, the family, contact and partner preferences.
tradition.jain.symbol: Families print the Jain symbol, the Ahimsa hand or the Namokar Mantra at the top. The line at the top takes any words you type, such as “Jai Jinendra”.
tradition.jain.tip.1: Write Digambar or Shwetambar, and your community (such as Oswal, Porwal or Agarwal) in Caste.
tradition.jain.tip.2: Many families mention a vegetarian or Jain diet in Partner preferences.
tradition.jain.tip.3: Leave out the horoscope rows if your family doesn't use them: hide them and they won't print.
guide.metaTitle: What to write in a marriage biodata: a part-by-part guide
guide.metaDescription: What to write in each part of a marriage biodata: personal details, horoscope, education and career, family, contact, about me, partner preferences and the photo.
guide.title: What to write in each part of your biodata
guide.lead: A biodata is read quickly, often on a phone, by people who don't know you yet. Keep each part short, true and easy to scan. Here is what families usually write, with examples from a fictional biodata.
guide.personal.title: Personal details
guide.personal.text: Your full name as you want it printed, date of birth, height, and where you were born and live. Add complexion, mother tongue or marital status only if your family usually prints them.
guide.personal.example: Name: Sai Teja Mandapati · Date of Birth: 13-01-1998 · Height: 5' 8"
guide.horoscope.title: Horoscope
guide.horoscope.text: If your family matches horoscopes, give the exact time and place of birth, the nakshatra with its pada, the rashi and the gotra. If it doesn't, hide these rows: hidden rows never print.
guide.horoscope.example: Time of Birth: 10:55 PM · Nakshatra: Pushya (3rd Pada) · Rashi: Karka · Gotra: Bharadwaja
guide.education.title: Education and career
guide.education.text: Your highest qualification with the college, then what you do and where. A yearly income is common but optional; write it the way your family is comfortable with.
guide.education.example: Qualification: B.Tech (Computer Science), Sample Institute of Engineering · Occupation: Software Engineer, Example Technologies, Hyderabad
guide.family.title: Family
guide.family.text: One line per person: name, what they do and where they live. Parents first, then brothers and sisters with their spouses, then grandparents or anyone else your family usually lists. Write “(Late)” before a name where it applies.
guide.family.example: Father: Mandapati Venkata Rao, Sri Sai Traders · Brother (Elder): Mandapati Rahul, Staff Engineer, California
guide.contact.title: Contact
guide.contact.text: One or two phone numbers that someone will answer, often a parent's, and the town or full address. A number can carry a short note, such as Father or Mother.
guide.about.title: About me
guide.about.text: Two or three sentences in your own words: what you're like, what you enjoy and what matters to you. Plain and warm beats clever.
guide.about.example: I am calm and cheerful, enjoy cooking and weekend cricket, and value honesty and time with family.
guide.partner.title: Partner preferences
guide.partner.text: A few lines on what matters to you in a partner: values, education, where you'd like to live. Keep it kind and open; a long list of conditions puts people off.
guide.partner.example: Someone kind, family-minded and independent, who enjoys travel and simple living.
guide.photo.title: Photo
guide.photo.text: A recent, clear photo from the chest up, in daylight, facing the camera, against a plain background. Crop it in the app so the face sits in the upper part of the frame. More photos can go on pages of their own.
guide.before.title: Before you send it
guide.before.text: Check names and numbers once more, look at the whole page in the preview, and ask someone in the family to read it. Download the PDF for printing and sharing; save a picture for chats.
